summary: Host only; nothing flashed or run on the phone in this task and no jump made. Native run 006 (decision 0014, loader-diag-trig-hold-adt8-aln) reached the held PRE_JUMP (mask 0x01ff, no exception). NAT-028 prepares the remainder of goal step 4 on the host: loader-diag-xnu-entry (build-008) keeps the loader unchanged up to the cache clean and then, instead of holding at PRE_JUMP, jumps through start.S's existing br x16 to the entry of the kernel copy, where a 40-byte position-independent stub (xnu_stub.S) written by the loader draws STAGE 0x50 and holds. Entry facts are derived from the payload header (virt_base 0xfffffff004000000, entry_va 0xfffffff00743b4a8, segment 2, payload offset 0x437898; entry word 14000aed = b #0xfffffff00743e05c followed by 725 NOP words before the next real instruction), not from the loader log; expected PC = window base + 0x343b4a8 and x0 - PC = 0x153cb58. The installer (xnu_entry.c) overwrites word 0 plus nine NOPs only and refuses (writes nothing) when the entry is not 8-byte aligned, fewer than 0x28 file-backed bytes remain, a word after word 0 is not a NOP or the template is bad; it stores aligned 32-bit words, word 0 last, before the full-window clean. No XNU instruction is executed: the kernel's first word is replaced and not replayed; replaying it and continuing into XNU is a separate, not-built step. New marker kind XNU (10) and mask bit 10; mk_xnu_report exists only with MK_XNU_ENTRY=1; decode.py reports xnu_stub_pc / xnu_stub_x0. Host checks (test_nat022.py, 45 tests): stub bytes decoded by an independent field decoder, a decoder-driven interpreter of the installed stub on the real kernel entry bytes and capstone (venv only); the real installer compiled with gcc -fsanitize=alignment (trap mode) on the real entry bytes changes only the 40 stub bytes and every refusal case leaves bytes untouched; build test whitelists the loader.c diff (one removed HOLD line, 12 added lines), start.S diff exactly one '.globl _stack_top', other sources byte-identical, same SWEETXNU payload bytes, scan_unaligned 0; three mutation checks (wrong sp register, dropped NOP check, 64-bit literal store) were each detected. Builds: build-008 and build-008-repro agree; all eight earlier images and payloads keep their hashes (build-006); loader-diag-xnu-entry Image 6cb6b1a03a008a40de6ebe5e823e773000b0a3e4899f9263f06adf4a41b2bcc3 (217088 bytes), Image.payload d4c391624ad8d50ce4c629d905a7a8fa88da142118ec2ff6a548bbeef9658f27 (21771872 bytes), RECOVERY package-008 4353546c4494c2aad12eaf3b0188478f4157ee5e4e3658fd253387b80416d06a (payload verbatim at offset 2048). session_xnu.py is gated on docs/decisions/0015-nat022-loader-diag-xnu-entry-single-run-2026-11-10.md, which does not exist: it stopped with 0 adb commands. Not shown by this evidence: that the S24 fetches and runs code at the kernel copy entry (never tried), I-cache/fetch coherence after the loader's clean and ic iallu, the actual RAM window (implied ~0x9dd3fc000 from run 006, never read directly), behaviour after the 83 s watchdog, that nothing in the window is unlisted firmware memory, ADT/boot_args correctness for XNU, and any XNU instruction executing. A PRE_JUMP-or-0x50 frame is a statement about the loader's handoff path, not about XNU.
